display.purpose: The sidebar wordmark and global h1. A masthead — tight leading, negative tracking. Never a section heading.

body.purpose: Article prose. Serif, capped at a 65ch measure — non-negotiable.

label.purpose: The margin layer: mono metadata, dates, tags, badges. Uppercase, 0.08em tracking.

shadows.name: press-rest
shadows.purpose: Hard offset, no blur, no alpha. The element sits above the paper like a physical key.

shadows.name: press-hover
shadows.purpose: Paired with translate(2px, 2px): the element travels INTO its own shadow.

shadows.name: press-active
shadows.purpose: Paired with translate(4px, 4px): fully pressed, flat on the paper.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: The press. A little mechanical overshoot on buttons.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for opacity/transform state changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: A key to be pressed, not a CTA to be sold. Press it and it travels into its own shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 0.875rem 1.5rem; background: var(--color-canvas, #f4f1eb); color: var(--color-ink, #2c2a28); border: 2px solid var(--color-ink, #2c2a28); border-radius: 1px; font-family: "Public Sans", sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--color-stone, #d1ccc5); transition: background-color .2s cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.1), color .2s cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.1), transform .2s cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.1), box-shadow .2s cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.1); } .ds-btn:hover { background: var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); border-color: var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); color: var(--color-canvas, #f4f1eb); transform: translate(2px, 2px); box-shadow: 2px 2px 0 var(--color-stone, #d1ccc5); } .ds-btn:active { transform: translate(4px, 4px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 var(--color-stone, #d1ccc5); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Post-type Chip
components.description: Tints its own backdrop from currentColor — so the text colour also sets the fill. Uses the AA-safe cloudberry, never the display one.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; line-height: 1.4; padding: 0.1em 0.4em; border-radius: 2px; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--color-cloudberry-text, #984200); border: 1px solid currentColor; background-color: color-mix(in oklab, currentColor 10%, transparent); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Nav Item
components.description: The softest geometry in the system (4px), because it is the thing you aim at. 44px minimum target, enforced by test.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid transparent; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--color-ink, #2c2a28); text-decoration: none; transition: transform .2s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), background-color .2s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-nav:hover { background: var(--color-canvas-alt, #e9e5de); transform: translateX(2px); } .ds-nav[aria-current="page"] { border-color: var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); color: var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); } .ds-nav:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: URL Input
components.description: Mono, because it is data being entered — not prose. Hairline stone stroke; focus ring never suppressed.
components.css: .ds-input { width: min(100%, 30rem); padding: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--color-stone, #d1ccc5); border-radius: 1px; background: var(--color-canvas, #f4f1eb); color: var(--color-ink, #2c2a28); font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-size: 0.85rem; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-falu-red, #8c2121); outline-offset: 1px; }

components.description: Delimited by rules, not radii. Never floats — the hover state changes the surface, it does not lift.

narrative.overview:
A technical record, kept by hand, and warmed by the paper it's kept on. The page is ruled like engineering grid paper. The margins are annotated in monospace — dates, tags, reply-verbs, syndication links — while the prose itself is set in a serif and left alone to be read. The mono is the annotation layer; the serif is the record. Keeping those two voices distinct is the whole system.

This is not a terminal and not a document viewer. Every technical signal is held against warmth that comes from material and culture, not from a beige background: falu red is the pigment on Swedish barns, cloudberry is a Nordic berry. That specificity is what keeps the system out of the cream-and-serif lane it would otherwise fall into.
keyCharacteristics: Grid-paper ground; monospace margins; serif prose. Three voices, never blurred.
Near-square geometry (1-6px radii). Structure is carried by borders, never by soft shadows.
Depth is physical: hard, unblurred offsets that you press an element into.
Fluid everything — type and spacing scale with the viewport via clamp().
Two full themes. Dark is designed, not inverted.

rules.name: The Earned Warmth Rule
rules.body: The canvas tint carries no warmth on its own — it is a ground. Warmth is earned by falu red, cloudberry, and the serif. Audit test: strip the accents and the serif; if it still reads warm and editorial, the warmth was coming from the beige, and the beige is generic.

rules.name: The Two Cloudberries Rule
rules.body: --color-cloudberry is for borders and display; --color-cloudberry-text is for small text. The display colour fails WCAG AA below ~18px. Enforced by test/token-contrast.spec.js, including against the hover surface axe cannot reach.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Falu red is the only accent that gets to be loud, and it stays under ~10% of any view.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif = the record. Sans = the chrome. Mono = the margin. A voice used for the wrong job is a bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The 65ch Rule
rules.body: Article text never exceeds a 65ch measure, at any viewport. Reading is the product.

rules.name: The Displacement Rule
rules.body: Depth is communicated by displacement, never diffusion. Shadows are hard offsets — never blurred, never translucent — and interactive depth is movement: press an element and it travels into its own shadow. Audit test: if a box-shadow contains a blur radius or an rgba(), it does not belong in this system.

dos: Do keep the three voices separate: serif for prose, sans for chrome, mono for the margin.
Do cap article measure at 65ch. Reading is the product.
Do express depth as displacement — hard 4px 4px 0 offsets and a real press.
Do use --color-cloudberry-text (#984200) for any cloudberry text, and plain --color-cloudberry only for borders and display.
Do give links inside prose a non-colour cue (an underline). Colour alone is never the carrier.
Do design dark mode as its own theme. It is not an inversion.
Do let structure be carried by borders — 2px ink, 1px stone.
donts: Don't add a blurred or translucent box-shadow. If it has a blur radius or an rgba(), it is not this system.
Don't deepen the background to make the page feel warmer. The beige earns nothing.
Don't put raw --color-cloudberry on small text. It fails WCAG AA and the build will fail with it.
Don't give the sidebar an inner scrollbar. Ever.
Don't reach for pills, rounded-lg, gradient CTAs, stock hero illustration, or "Book a demo" — that is the corporate dev-marketing blog.
Don't add signup modals, interstitials, or "clap"-style affordances over the content — that is the siloed blog platform this site exists to be the opposite of.
Don't go monospace-everything and black-on-white. That is the brutalist/terminal dev blog — the near miss.
Don't ship generated prose, SEO filler, or stock imagery. That is the AI-slop content farm, and the notbyai badge is a standing promise against it.
